title: IDCAMS DEFINE CLUSTER with LINEAR and ZFS: data sets with no record structure
shapes: AIXA jcl/AIXADF3.jcl IDC010: DEFINE CLUSTER (NAME(PROD.AIXA.EXTRACT) LINEAR CONTROLINTERVALSIZE(4096) ...)
AIXA jcl/AIXADF3.jcl IDC010: DEFINE CLUSTER (NAME(PROD.AIXA.REPORTS.ZFS) ZFS CYLINDERS(5 1))
asserts: Two jcl_utility_cards facts with verb DEFINE of step IDC010 of AIXADF3, one per card. The LINEAR card defines PROD.AIXA.EXTRACT, a linear data set; the ZFS card defines PROD.AIXA.REPORTS.ZFS, a linear data set that is a z/OS UNIX zFS file system. Neither is a KSDS, RRDS or ESDS: neither card carries KEYS or RECORDSIZE, and no COBOL SELECT reads either data set, so no program organization corresponds to these kinds (unlike INDEXED, NUMBERED and NONINDEXED of H-0082).

citations.doc: z/OS DFSMS Access Method Services Commands (z/OS 2.5.0), DEFINE CLUSTER Optional Parameters
citations.quote: Specifies that the cluster being defined is for linear data.

citations.doc: z/OS DFSMS Access Method Services Commands (z/OS 2.5.0), DEFINE CLUSTER Optional Parameters
citations.quote: All restrictions and conditions applicable to linear data sets apply to ZFS CLUSTERs.

notes: The ZFS definition (a z/OS UNIX zFS file system) is on the same page; only the restriction sentence is quoted verbatim. CONTROLINTERVALSIZE(4096) is legal (the page rounds a linear data set's size up to a 4096 multiple); the key asserts the cards, not the rounding. The DEFINE CLUSTER overview page carries only the syntax table, so the parameter page is cited.
